reconstruction:
I rebuilt the argument from the verified bytes in nine steps, recomputing rather than reading along wherever a number appears.

(1) Model and reference. The field is centred Gaussian on the side-24 torus with K(x) = k(x1)k(x2) and k the periodised Gaussian normalised to k(0)=1. I recomputed a_2 = -k''(0) and k''''(0) from the image sums: a_2 = 1 and k''''(0) = 3 to double precision, the planar values, the periodisation correction being of order e^{-288}. The reference law Q(v) = Q6 (x) Q_y^0(v) with Q_y^0(v) = N((-v,-v,0)^T, diag(2,2,1)) is exactly the planar one-point conditional Hessian law: conditioning fxx on f=v shifts its mean by -a_2 v = -v and its variance from k''''(0)=3 to 3 - a_2^2 = 2, Hxy has variance 1, and Cov(fxx,fyy|f) = 1 - 1 = 0, which is why the reference factorises. The object keeps Q6 EXACT and only idealises the y-block, and it says so.

(2) Chi-square lemma (1). I verified the equality log(1+chi^2) = -(1/2)log det(I-E^2) + m^T(I-E)^{-1}m by computing int p^2/q directly: in one dimension with E=0, m=0.3 it gives e^{m^2}, and with m=0, e=0.2 it gives (1-e^2)^{-1/2}; a Jacobi-eigenvalue implementation of the closed form agrees with Simpson quadrature to 1e-9 (0.132910997260 both ways). The stated bound follows from -log(1-x) <= x/(1-x) with sum e_i^2 = delta^2 and ||(I-E)^{-1}||_op <= (1-delta)^{-1}; on 200 random symmetric (m,E) with delta < 1 the bound held every time, worst case LHS/RHS = 0.978.

(3) Typed saddle moments (2). Under Q_y^0, U=(Hxx+Hyy)/2 ~ N(-v,1), V=(Hxx-Hyy)/2 and B=Hxy are standard and independent, det H = U^2 - T with T = V^2+B^2 ~ chi-square(2), so g = (T-U^2)_+. Memorylessness of T gives E(T-c)_+ = 2e^{-c/2} and E(T-c)_+^2 = 8e^{-c/2}; I reproduced both by quadrature at c = 0, 0.7, 3.1. Integrating over U gives m_0(v) = sqrt2 e^{-v^2/4} and E_Q g^2 = 4 m_0(v); quadrature gives 0.986663322476234 against the formula's 0.986663322476286, and 3.946653289904935 against 4 m_0 = 3.946653289905143.

(4) The weighted comparison (3). W and g are independent UNDER Q because Q is a product law, so ||Wg||_2 = ||W||_2 ||g||_2 exactly - no Holder is used across the three determinants. Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||W||_2 <= h_2 after dropping the typing indicators, ||g||_2 = 2 sqrt(m_0(v)), and |E_P(Wg) - Z m_0(v)| = |E_Q[(L-1)Wg]| <= ||L-1||_2 ||Wg||_2 gives eta. The substitutions Z >= Z_lo and m_0(v) >= m_{0,min} = sqrt2 e^{-b^2/4} are in the conservative direction because m_0 decreases in v on the positive mark window.

(5) Covariance construction (4)-(5). U = L_c^{-1}C and R = L_h^{-1}(H - XG^{-1}C) are the standard whitening of the pins and of the pair-Hessian residual, so Cov(U)=Cov(R)=I and Cov(U,R)=0. The blocks are then textbook Gaussian conditioning: Sigma_pp = I - FD^{-1}F^T is Cov(R|C,Y), Sigma_py = (J - FD^{-1}C_y^T)W_y is Cov(R,H_y|C,Y) in W_y-whitened coordinates, and Sigma_yy subtracts both T^T T (conditioning on C) and C_y D^{-1} C_y^T (conditioning on Y). The mean displacement m_y is E[H_y|C,Y] minus the reference mean (-v,-v,0), which is exactly why the term v(C_y D^{-1} e_0 + (1,1,0)^T) appears. I checked each block against the conditioning identity rather than against the object's prose.

(6) Y-density ratio (6)-(7). D = E0 - B^TB <= E0 gives det E0/det D <= (1-beta)^{-3}, hence the (1-beta)^{-3/2} density factor, and D <= E0 gives D^{-1} >= E0^{-1}, which is what licenses replacing the quadratic form of w - muY by the E0 one in the upper bound. The lower bound (7) is not a loosened estimate: (b^2 beta + 2bu + u^2)/(1-beta) equals 2bu + u^2 + beta(b+u)^2/(1-beta) identically, which I confirmed as an exact rational identity on 500 random (b,u,beta), so (7) is precisely the assembled bound.

(7) Integration. rho_ref(v) = p_{E0,0}(v,0,0) m_0(v) = e^{-3v^2/4}/(2 pi^{3/2} a_2) - I checked the algebra including the det(E0)^{1/2} = a_2 factor. Because the final bound is a single global sup and inf of rho/rho_ref times the reference integral, the mark integral is closed form: J_ref = [erf(sqrt3 b/2) - erf(sqrt3 (b-r^3/6)/2)]/(2 pi sqrt3 a_2). Evaluated at 80 decimal digits with a Taylor expansion about the window midpoint, I get 6.3529298594549898873523e-7 against the object's 6.3529298594549898874e-7 - agreement to 20 significant digits. The far part of [-12,12]^2 has area 576 - 25 pi = 497.460183660255169, and 12 sqrt2 = 16.97 < 17, so the certified annulus does contain the whole far square.

(8) Headline. area x J_ref = 3.16034...e-4; the object's unrounded endpoints 0.00027817807867916 and 0.00035413986017516 correspond to ratios 0.880218550 and 1.120578860, which sit just inside the displayed 0.88021 and 1.12058, i.e. the displayed ratios are rounded outward as claimed. Dividing by r^3 = 1.25e-4 gives 2.225424629 and 2.833118881, whose outward roundings are exactly the headline 2.22542 and 2.83312.

(9) Internal consistency of the certified table. This is the strongest structural check available without the code. Feeding the tabulated ||E||_F < 0.043544631 and ||m|| < 0.008864422 into lemma (1) yields chi^2 <= 1.032557e-3, which is the tabulated chi-square row to seven significant digits; feeding h_2 < 0.014009957, that chi-square, Z_lo and m_{0,min} = 0.986663322476286 into (3) yields eta = 0.116820011 against the tabulated 0.116819988; and (1 + eta) x 1.003365693 = 1.1205789, whose outward rounding is the tabulated 1.12058. The table is therefore not a collection of independent assertions: four of its rows are recomputable from three others plus the imported floor.

findings.criterion: RN5 determinant-moment erratum, scope of the far-region proof
findings.statement: The documented claim that RN3's far-region proof is outside the RN5 affected scope is CONFIRMED for sections 1-8, and confirmed for a reason stronger than the one the repository gives. The RN5 defect was an exponent-selection error inside a Holder(4,4,2) envelope across three determinants. RN3 never applies Holder across the three determinants at all: W (the pair factor) and g (the y factor) are independent under the product reference law Q, so ||Wg||_2 = ||W||_2 ||g||_2 is an identity, and the y factor enters as the EXACT second moment E_Q g^2 = 4 m_0(v), which I re-derived and reproduced by quadrature. The pair factor h_2 = (E(det H_M)^4 E(det H_S)^4)^{1/4} is exactly the factor the CORRECT Holder(4,4,2) also carries, so it is not the defective substitution either.
findings.evidence: Quadrature: E_Q g^2 = 3.946653289904935 against 4 m_0 = 3.946653289905143; m_0(1.2) = 0.986663322476234 against sqrt2 e^{-0.36} = 0.986663322476286. Sensitivity control NC2: substituting sqrt(E_Q g^4) = sqrt(192 m_0) for sqrt(E_Q g^2) moves eta from 0.116820011 to 0.809352777 and the far ratio to 1.815443, breaking the object's own 0.6798 budget - so the correct exponent is load-bearing and its use here is a property of the argument, not an accident of scale.

findings.criterion: RN5 determinant-moment erratum, scope of section 9
findings.statement: The same claim is NOT true of the whole object. Section 9's conditional arithmetic imports the near target 17.6804 r^3, and docs/RESEARCH_MAP.md section 3 records that the older published 17.6804 r^3 used a different mark-cap heuristic and sits beside the wrong-power diagnostic 17.67237 r^3, against a corrected diagnostic of about 2.34195 r^3 - a factor of about 7.5. So the displayed sum I_near + I_far < 20.51352 r^3 is built from a number the RN5 repair places inside, or immediately adjacent to, the affected scope. The repository sentence 'RN3's far-region proof is outside the affected scope' is accurate about the far-region proof and about nothing else in this file; a consumer who reads it as covering the object as a whole will carry the 20.51352 r^3 figure out of the affected scope by mistake. The object does hedge the line as 'Conditional arithmetic only' and 'not presently a full remote certificate', which is why this is MAJOR and not BLOCKING.
findings.evidence: Object section 9, verified bytes. docs/RESEARCH_MAP.md lines 179-186. 17.6804 + 2.83312 = 20.51352 exactly, so the sum is arithmetically what it claims to be; the objection is to the provenance of its first term, not its addition.

findings.criterion: Uniformity of the bounds claimed uniform
findings.statement: Every bound the object calls certified is genuinely a sup-over-region statement and not a pointwise one, in the only sense the argument needs: lemma (1) is applied with a single delta and a single ||m|| valid on the whole domain, and the final integral uses one global sup and one global inf of rho/rho_ref times the reference integral, so no per-box quadrature and no interchange of sup and integral is involved. The uniformity is over (y,v) in 5 <= |y| <= 17 times [b-r^3/6, b] at the single rung r = 1/20 and the single axis orientation. It is NOT uniform in r, not over endpoint orientations, and not over the near zone, and the object says so in its own closing paragraph.

The certificate is, numerically, a statement at v = b. This matters because 'complete mark window' reads as substantive coverage, and a consumer could take it as evidence of robustness that the object has not demonstrated.

findings.criterion: Spatial cover: membership rule does not reproduce the stated count
findings.statement: The text says the cover is 'every quarter-unit Cartesian box intersecting the closed annulus' with membership by 'exact integer inequalities against 25 and 289'. That rule, applied literally, selects 13,612 boxes, not the 13,604 the object states and the register carries. The difference is exactly the 8 boxes whose maximum squared radius equals 25 exactly, i.e. the ones that meet the closed annulus only at a corner on the inner circle, at (+-3,+-4) and (+-4,+-3); the stated count corresponds to a strict inner comparison. I checked the consequence and it is benign - each excluded box shares that single corner with an included neighbour, so the domain remains covered and the uniform bounds are untouched - but a replayer cannot reproduce 13,604 from the rule as written, and the box count is one of the object's own runtime gates. The text should state the strict inner inequality.

Lemma (1) is an identity plus two elementary inequalities; (2) is exact Gaussian integration; (7) is an exact rearrangement rather than a loosened estimate; the ten-term trace truncation carries a rigorous remainder; J_ref is closed form and reproduces to 20 significant digits; the area and the final arithmetic reproduce exactly; the algorithmic parameters (384 bits, degree-28 grouped Taylor, quarter-unit boxes, ten trace terms) all carry rigorous enclosures rather than tuned tolerances. does_not_establish:
This record is a verdict on 12,956 bytes and nothing else. Specifically, it does not establish any of the following.

1. It does not establish that the far-region bound 2.22542 r^3 < I_far < 2.83312 r^3 is true. The three interval-run constants that carry the whole quantitative claim - ||E||_F < 0.043544631, ||m|| < 0.008864422, h_2 < 0.014009957 - were not replayed, because I did not obtain the 2.6 MB bundle. What I verified is that IF those three numbers and the imported floor Z_lo hold, THEN everything the object derives from them follows, and the table's own rows agree with each other to seven significant digits. A 0.1% error in one of those three inputs would break the chi-square row.

2. It does not verify the 294 audit checks, the 24 full nine-pin Gaussian laws, the covariance floors, the image-tail and spectral-tail enclosures, the degree-28 grouped Taylor remainders, the Arb runtime, the -O gate behaviour, or the normal-versus-optimized replay agreement.

3. It does not confirm the Kac-Rice integrand. If rho(y,v) is not the right integrand for the W-weighted endpoint Palm count, everything in this review is a correct analysis of the wrong quantity, and the object supplies no identity by which to check it.

4. It establishes nothing about the near annulus 0.1 <= |y| <= 5, nothing about the disc |y| < 0.1, nothing about any r other than 1/20, nothing about other endpoint orientations, and nothing about chart integration. It does not act on D3-LEMMA-RN-UNIF Piece 1 or Piece 2, on OBL-H5-JETMOD, OBL-H5-ZBAND, OBL-H5-REMOTE-THRESHOLD, PERC-DECAY, OBL-B1-BRANCH or B4.loc; every one of those obligations stands exactly as it stood before.

5. It creates no organizational independence and no fraction of any. RV-RN3's Independence status remains EXTERNAL_REVIEW_OPEN, its Reviewer/claim column remains UNASSIGNED, and no register was edited by this review. The technical verdict AMEND is not a step toward the independence predicate; it is orthogonal to it.

6. My confirmation that sections 1-8 are outside the RN5 affected scope covers the exponent structure of the argument, which I checked and which is correct, and does NOT cover the implementation of the fourth determinant moments inside rn_joint.py, which I never saw. It also does not extend to section 9, where I found the opposite.

7. Nothing here composes the 2D upper and lower tracks with the 3D lifetime track; the object is a 2D far-zone intensity bound at one rung and must not be joined to the 3D result.
